title: I Enforced the Table-Tennis Paddle Reservation on the Club Who Booked Ghosts

parts.text: I reserved table 3 at 6:48 p.m. and club duo Ellis had a ghost hour still lit on my paddle card. The kiosk said: BOOK THE TABLE. ONE HOUR. NO GHOST NAMES. I was thirty-four, rec member, holding a card. Ellis shrugged. "Clubs are the rubber." I photographed the kiosk, the card, and the ghost name. Then I asked for the table log. At 6:54 rec staff pinged why Ellis's name was on a ghost hour. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Rec staff can see Ellis's ghost hour still lit on table 3 during my reservation.

social.video_title: The club booked a ghost hour on my paddle card — Part 1/2
social.description: Table tennis, a kiosk hold, a ghost name. I logged the hour. Would you have asked rec staff?

parts.text: Ellis called it warmup until rec asked for the still. I printed the log, the kiosk, and the card. The ghost dropped. Ellis booked real names and told the next club warmup was always about optics. Optics is a word clubs use when kiosks exist. Reservation now has a second line: GHOSTS ARE NOT RUBBER. I keep table 3. Ellis brown-bags the jokes. The rec finally looks like a card, not a rumor. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Table log, dropped ghost, and a second line. Was warmup ever my card?
